concepts.title: Hard Work versus Magic Shortcuts
concepts.section: A Bottle of Dew, Let us read
concepts.definition: The theme of the story is that real wealth grows from patient labour, not from any magical shortcut. Rama Natha chases a potion that turns things to gold, yet the plantation he tends along the way earns the gold for him.
concepts.formula: theme = hard work + patience, not magic
concepts.key_idea: The sage's trick makes Rama Natha work his land for six years; the banana crop, not magic, creates the wealth.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr101.txt, A Bottle of Dew, Let us read

concepts.title: Rama Natha and Madhumati: Character Study
concepts.section: A Bottle of Dew, Let us read
concepts.definition: Rama Natha begins as a dreamer who wastes his inheritance chasing a magic potion and grows into a hardworking farmer. Madhumati is the practical, worried wife whose market sense turns the banana crop into money.
concepts.key_idea: Rama Natha changes from a dreamer into a willing worker, while Madhumati supports him by selling the fruit.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr101.txt, A Bottle of Dew, Let us read

concepts.title: Sequence of Story Events
concepts.section: A Bottle of Dew, Let us read and reflect
concepts.definition: The story runs in a fixed order: a lazy heir hears of a potion, plants banana plants to gather dew, collects five litres over six years, and learns the trick only when the potion fails but a box of gold coins appears.
concepts.key_idea: Ordering events, like giving the bottle to the sage before the failure of the potion, shows how the plot builds to the reveal.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr101.txt, A Bottle of Dew, Let us read and reflect

solution_steps.explain: List the events that move the story forward, each in a few words.

concepts.title: Word Meanings in Context: Potion, Dew and Chant
concepts.section: A Bottle of Dew, Let us learn
concepts.definition: New words are understood from the sentence around them: a potion is a liquid with magical properties, dew is night moisture on leaves, and to chant is to repeat a word or phrase again and again.
concepts.key_idea: Context clues around a new word, like leaves and night for dew, give its meaning without a dictionary.
concepts.textbook_ref: fepr101.txt, A Bottle of Dew, Let us learn
question_patterns: what does the word potion mean in the story

solution_steps.action: find the word in its line
solution_steps.explain: Locate the sentence where the new word appears.
Read before and after the word to see what sense the sentence needs.
Swap in the guessed meaning; if the sentence still makes sense, the meaning is right.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did the sage play a trick on Rama Natha?

solution_template.explain: The sage says a direct truth would not have been believed by Rama Natha.

solution_template.action: state the purpose of the trick
solution_template.explain: Only six years of work on the plantation could show Rama Natha that effort, not magic, makes money.

worked_examples.source_ref: fepr101.txt, Let us think and reflect I.2(i)
worked_examples.question_pattern: Put these in order: the sage smiled; the bottle was given; drops fell on the vessel; words were murmured; the wait began.

solution_template.explain: Rama Natha must hand over the bottle before anything else can happen.
The sage smiles, mutters over the water, returns it; then drops fall on the copper vessel and the wait begins.
